body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Saturday, August 22, 2026 — a hot one, with a high near 103° and air quality at moderate (AQI 64). Overnight, a shooting outside a Taco Bell in east Bakersfield was the most serious call. Our top story this morning: McFarland police are investigating a homicide after a 26-year-old man was shot and killed at the Capri Laundromat on Perkins Avenue. Let’s get you caught up.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most serious call came just after midnight, when a witness reported seeing someone shot at a Taco Bell in the Baker Street area. Officers responded with an officer-safety broadcast after the witness described the suspect as a white male in his 40s to 50s, wearing a black shirt and dark pants, sitting inside a white vehicle — possibly a Ford Explorer. Earlier, around 2:16 a.m., crews knocked down a fire at a vacant house on King Street, where flames were visible inside the single-story structure with heavy smoke showing. Multiple engines and a truck company responded, and the fire was under control by about 2:25. Just before 11 p.m., a two-vehicle collision left one vehicle on fire near Gosford Road and Harris Road. Engine 14 and Engine 9 responded — one car was smoking with another about a quarter mile back — and command dubbed it the Harris Incident. Injuries were unknown. Multiple reports of a grass fire drew a large response — engines, patrol units, a water tender, a dozer and a helicopter — to southbound Highway 395 north of Brown Road. Crews found a small roadside fire that was quickly extinguished, and the extra equipment was canceled. Around 10:38 p.m., an assault with a knife was reported with no injuries. The suspect — about 6 feet tall with neck tattoos, wearing black shorts, a gray shirt and white shoes — fled on foot northbound.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 103° and a low around 75° tonight. It’s currently 97° at Meadows Field (KBFL). There are no active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is 64 — moderate.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that McFarland police are investigating a homicide after a 26-year-old man was shot and killed Saturday afternoon at the Capri Laundromat in the 100 block of Perkins Avenue.** Officers responded to the scene at approximately 3:18 p.m. and found the man suffering from multiple gunshot wounds inside the laundromat. Officers immediately provided medical aid and initiated CPR, but the victim was pronounced dead at the scene. Preliminary information indicates two unknown suspects arrived at the Capri Liquors in the 100 block of Perkins Avenue and confronted the victim inside the Capri Laundromat, which is adjacent to the gas pumps. An argument led to one of the suspects producing a firearm and shooting the victim multiple times. The two suspects then fled the area in an unknown vehicle. No suspects have been identified, no arrests have been made, and the motive remains unknown. The victim’s identity will be released after next of kin have been notified. McFarland Police Department detectives are actively working the scene and gathering investigative information. Police say there is no current threat to the community, but the public is advised to avoid the area until the scene is processed. Anyone with information about this investigation is asked to call Detective Galvan or Detective Cazares at 661-792-2121.

**According to 23ABC, a deadly shooting at an Independence High School football game left nearby residents shaken, and a 15-year-old suspect was arrested miles away from the scene.** The scene at Independence High School was chaotic as people tried to understand what had happened after gunshots rang out nearby. Erin Foster lives a few houses down from where the suspect was arrested. She said she was in shock when she learned what had happened. “I like our little neighborhood. That’s kind of scary. I have, like, goosebumps. That’s kind of scary. And he’s 15. Oh, my.” Foster said. Foster said she was on her way to her fiancé’s workplace when she noticed an unusual scene outside her home. “We couldn’t get out of the garage. There was, like, a little Hispanic family sitting over here on. I’m sorry, on the side of the garage, but there were a cop car in these undercover cars, and I was like, ‘We can’t get out.’ So we had to ask him to move, but it was just odd ‘cause then they were still here when I came back.” Foster said. She said the family remained outside for an extended period of time. “Just odd that there was, like, a little Hispanic family, like a little baby, and like a mom it looked like, and some two, like, toddler little girls, and it was just like, ‘Why are they sitting on the side of my garage?’” Foster said.

**KGET 17 reports that Bakersfield Mayor Karen Goh has released a statement on the deadly shooting at Independence High School.** Mayor Goh said, “I am deeply saddened and angered by the senseless act of violence that occurred last night at the Independence High School football game. My thoughts are with the victim’s family and friends during this incredibly difficult time. I want to thank the Bakersfield Police Department for their swift response and apprehension of the suspect. As a mother and as your mayor, I am committed to doing everything in my power to ensure our community is safe and that our children can attend school events without fear. We will continue to work with our law enforcement partners to hold those responsible accountable and to prevent future tragedies.”

**KGET 17 tells us that a 15-year-old has been arrested in connection to the deadly shooting at Independence High School.** Bakersfield police said the 15-year-old suspect was arrested miles away from the scene. Police said the suspect was located and arrested in the 1000 block of West Columbus Street. The suspect’s name has not been released due to his age. Police said the shooting happened during the football game between Independence High School and South High School. The victim was a 15-year-old boy who was not a student at either school. Police said the shooting appears to be gang-related.

**Bakersfield Now reports that Southwest Market has canceled its Saturday event at Independence High School after the fatal shooting.** The event was scheduled to take place from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. at the high school. Southwest Market said in a statement, “Due to the tragic incident that occurred last night at Independence High School, we have decided to cancel today’s Southwest Market event. Our thoughts and prayers are with the victim’s family and friends during this difficult time. We will provide more information about future events as it becomes available.”

**Bakersfield Now says a 15-year-old has been arrested in the deadly shooting at Independence High football game.** The arrest was made in the 1000 block of West Columbus Street. The suspect’s name has not been released. The victim was a 15-year-old boy who was not a student at either Independence or South high schools. The shooting happened during the football game.

**KGET 17 has a story on flesh-eating bacteria, warning of the signs to watch for.** The station reports that while rare, necrotizing fasciitis is a serious bacterial skin infection that spreads quickly and can be life-threatening. Symptoms include red or swollen skin, severe pain, fever, and ulcers or blisters. The bacteria most commonly enter the body through a cut, scrape, or other break in the skin. If you experience any of these symptoms, seek medical attention immediately. Early treatment with antibiotics is crucial to preventing the infection from spreading.

## Something good

A local family is organizing a flea market to help raise funds for a prosthetic leg. This community event aims to support a local resident in need. It’s a heartwarming example of neighbors coming together to lend a hand.

## Coming up this week

On Tuesday, August 26, the Bakersfield City Council will hold a special meeting at 12:00 p.m. followed by a regular meeting at 3:30 p.m. and another at 5:15 p.m. All meetings will take place at City Hall. On Saturday, August 23, Los Yonic’s Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio will perform at the Fox Theater. On Tuesday, August 26, the Fox Theater will offer a Cults & Classics: Season Pass 2026-2027. On Friday, August 29, Rodney Carrington will take the stage at the Fox Theater. On Saturday, August 30, CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE will be held at the Fox Theater. Also on Saturday, August 30, Willie Barcena will perform at the Fox Theater. And later that same day, Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix will be held at the Fox Theater.
